THE RULES OF THIS PARTICULAR UNIVERSE

You, a few seconds ago.

In local play, use the arrow keys or movement buttons. In Twitch mode, viewers type !up, !right, !down, !left, !wait, or !rewind. Each viewer has one vote per beat; a later command replaces their previous vote.

  1. Most votes wins. Ties and silent beats become a wait. Even when you wait, your echoes keep moving.
  2. Rewind to record. A copy of your route becomes an echo. It replays one recorded position per beat, then stays put. There are three echo slots; a fourth replaces the oldest.
  3. Switches open matching doors. A or B can be held by you or an echo. Echoes replay their recorded footprints exactly, even through a door that is now closed.
  4. Get the present to the exit. The lime robot must reach the portal. If the beat limit runs out first, the loop automatically rewinds.

The board is isometric. The little compass in its lower left shows how map directions appear on screen.

INVITE THE WHOLE TIMELINE

Put chat in the driver's seat.

Connect to a Twitch channel through EventSub. Echo Relay reads chat commands; it never posts messages.

Paste its client ID above, then sign in. Only the user:read:chat permission is requested. Do not paste a client secret.

Already have a user access token?

Access tokens stay in this tab's memory and are sent only to Twitch. They are never stored in a capsule or browser storage. Reloading requires reconnecting.

FIELD NOTES / 001

What if chat could
leave itself a hand?

Most audience games ask what chat wants to do next. Echo Relay asks what a crowd can do when its previous decisions become another player.

Each rewind makes a real, deterministic recording. Those recordings are not decoration: they occupy switches, open doors, and make otherwise unreachable exits possible. The crowd has to plan a favor for its future self.

A time capsule lets those favors cross streams. Export your community's echoes, send the small JSON file to another streamer, and let a new crowd finish the puzzle with your ghosts.
